overview.text: Indian Overseas Bank invites IRDAI-licensed Stand-Alone Health Insurance companies for a corporate agency tie-up to distribute health insurance products to its customers through branches and digital channels. The arrangement is initially for 3 years, renewable at the Bank's discretion for a further 3 years. Reference RFP/SAHI/003/2026-27, dated 11.05.2026.

summary.issuing_organization: Indian Overseas Bank; Marketing & Development Department, 763 Anna Salai, Central Office, Chennai-600002; Ref. RFP/SAHI/003/2026-27; queries: mdd@iob.bank.in, 044-28519639/ 044-71729204

scope.text: Corporate agency arrangement with one or more additional Stand-Alone Health Insurance companies to distribute individual and group health insurance products through branches and digital channels including internet banking and mobile banking.
Customise insurance products for every segment of the Bank's customers, with premiums in tune with market rates and competitive.
Support the Bank on sales, renewals, claims, customer complaint resolution, MIS, training, IT and manpower across the country.
Provide day-to-day data on policies issued, renewals, lapses and claims, with real-time data exchange with the Bank, and give the Bank portal access through a User ID and password.
Source business from all centres for the initial 01 year; permission for the subsequent 2 years may be extended by the Bank on satisfactory performance, subject to annual review.
Provide MIS updates on status of customer complaints on a weekly/fortnightly/monthly basis.
Settle claims without delay and within IRDAI timelines, run a grievance redressal procedure, issue renewal notices well before expiry, and issue policy documents and endorsements without delay.
Annexure 16 information security scope applies if data is hosted on the successful bidder's own premises (data centre).

key_requirements.text: Bid must meet every minimum eligibility criterion in Annexure-1; a proposal failing any one is rejected straight away.
Bidder must sign the Pre-Contract Integrity Pact (Annexure-17); a bidder not signing or refusing to sign is disqualified.
Bid must be submitted only through the Bank's e-tendering portal using a Class III Digital Certificate with signing and encryption; email, fax, post or courier bids are rejected.
Successful bidder must not sub-contract any part of the services without the Bank's prior written consent.
Successful bidder must inform the Bank within 24 hours of any regulatory breach, penalty, show cause or warning issued by IRDAI, SEBI, RBI or other regulators.
Successful bidder must bear all expenditure on integration of APIs, technology or system synchronisation, and comply with all applicable IRDAI regulations and guidelines.
Successful bidder must keep Bank customer data confidential and not use or disclose it for any purpose other than services under this RFP and the Agreement.
Successful bidder must provide online system access for MIS and MIS reports on business under the contract, and maintain policyholder records in safe custody.
AI/ML models used by the bidder must not be trained on Bank or Bank customer sensitive data and must be deployed on-premises by default; cloud or third-party AI needs the Bank's prior approval.
Bank must be notified within 4 hours of any suspected data breach from discovery; vulnerability assessment at least half-yearly and penetration testing at least yearly.

eligibility.text: Must hold a valid IRDAI insurance licence, valid on the date of RFP submission; copy of original licence and current licence with proof of renewal required.

Must be a government organization/PSU or a company registered under the Companies Act 1956 /2013 and with IRDAI, in existence for at least 5 years in standalone health insurance with business in India in the last 5 years.

Must have at least 3 years of experience in Bancassurance and a corporate agency tie-up with at least 2 Scheduled Commercial Banks, preferably 1 Public Sector Bank; certificate from beneficiary bank required.
Must have a minimum Claim Settlement Ratio of 90% in the last 2 financial years as on 31.03.2025 (FY24-25 and FY23-24).
Must have a minimum Solvency Ratio of 150% as on 31.03.2025 (C.A. certificate basis).
Must have minimum average Rs.5000 Crores underwritten premium (new business plus renewal) in the last 2 years.
Must sign the Integrity Pact (Annexure-17), a preliminary qualification; in a joint venture all partners must sign.

Must confirm in Annexure 15 that it is not blacklisted by any tie-up partner, PSU, PSB or private bank, has no pending cheating/fraud case, and has no IRDAI or other regulatory penalty or warning (details to be given if any).

important_dates.text: Last date for seeking clarification: 18.05.2026 (by 5.00 PM, by email to mdd@iob.bank.in).
Last date and time for receipt of proposals: 08.06.2026 up to 5.00 PM; no proposal is accepted after this.
Proposal validity: 180 days from the last date of submission.

commercial_requirements.text: Successful bidder pays the Bank remuneration/commission on each policy issued at mutually decided rates, within IRDAI regulations, on a monthly basis.
Commission must be remitted to the Bank by the 10th working day of every month with details of all policies issued till the end of the previous month.

Annexure-4 asks for maximum commission approved by IRDAI and maximum offered to the Bank per product; all commission must comply with IRDAI (Expenses of Management, including Commission, of Insurers) Regulations, 2024 (effective 01.04.2024).
Bank reserves the right to negotiate pricing/commission with the L1 insurance company anytime during the tenure of the agreement.
Bank may impose penalties and Liquidated Damages if performance is not as per its satisfaction; rate or cap not specified in the document.
Bank may set off any amount due to the Company and is not liable to pay damages to the Company in any condition.
Bidder bears all bid preparation costs and the cost of registration on the e-tendering portal.
EMD/bid security and Performance Bank Guarantee are mentioned in the Integrity Pact but no amount is stated anywhere; tender fee and warranty are not specified in the document.

project_duration.text: Tie-up is initially for a period of 3 years, subject to satisfactory performance and annual review; the Bank may renew for a further 3 years or discontinue.
Business sourcing from all centres is permitted for the initial 01 year, then 2 years more on satisfactory performance, subject to annual review.
Tie-up commencement date is to be determined or advised after the selection process is complete.
Integrity Pact is valid for 5 years or until complete execution of the contract including warranty, whichever is later; if the bidder is unsuccessful it expires six months after contract signing.

important_conditions.text: Evaluation: three stages - minimum eligibility (any failure rejects the proposal), technical evaluation carrying 70 marks, and a presentation carrying 30 marks.

Evaluation: technical scoring covers 14 parameters, maximum 70 marks in total, including solvency ratio, profit after tax, claim settlement ratio, Gross Written Premium, bank tie-ups, branches and penalties.
Evaluation: top shortlisted bidders on technical score are invited to present; the Bank decides the cut-off marks and the number of bidders; bidders bear their own travel and stay costs.
Submission: only via the e-tendering portal https://iobtenders.auctiontiger.net; the portal accepts no bids after the deadline and the acknowledgement must be kept.
Submission: data must be in the formats of Annexure 1 to Annexure 20, in English, in Indian Rupees, for the financial year ending March 31, 2025; other formats make the proposal non-compliant.
Submission: every page of the RFP document must be signed by the authorised person; bids with unsigned documents will be summarily rejected.
Submission: no overwriting, erasures or handwritten corrections; replies such as OK, accepted or noted are not acceptable.
Submission: verify the Class III Digital Certificate with the service provider at least two days before the due date; a mock drill is advised.

Risk: submission mode conflicts. The schedule and bid process allow submission only through the e-tendering portal, but one preface bullet says the bid in physical form with supporting documents should be submitted by the due date.
Risk: indemnity is uncapped, covering all actions, claims, losses and advocates' fees from repudiation or delay in settlement of claims or any matter connected with the agreement.
Risk: penalties and Liquidated Damages can be imposed at the Bank's satisfaction with no rate or cap stated; the Bank is not liable to pay damages to the Company.

Risk: the Bank may terminate by notice without assigning reason and the Company cannot terminate for convenience, while another clause says either party may terminate the tie-up per IRDAI Regulations.
Risk: suspected data breaches must be notified within 4 hours, and the provider bears financial losses or penalties up to an 'agreed Cap' that the document does not define.
Risk: how the 70 technical and 30 presentation marks combine into a final rank is not stated, yet award goes to the L1 bidder with commission negotiable afterwards.
